page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes an Intel processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, offering dedicated CPU allocation. The processor configuration includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. It features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, alongside Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the n4-standard-8 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently register in the middle 50 percent of tested systems. The instance demonstrates solid capabilities in cryptography and integer operations, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. However, certain memory-bound and multi-threaded tasks reveal performance limitations. The PassMark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks fall into the bottom 25 percent tier, indicating potential bottlenecks during intensive memory-subsystem operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced 1 to 4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance a standard option for workloads that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or high-speed local NVMe storage. It is suitable for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 12.95 GB per second, and database operations, as evidenced by its average PassMark database score and Redis SET throughput of 9.71 million operations per second. While it can handle light machine learning tasks like prompt processing for small 135M parameter models, it is poorly suited for larger LLM text generation, with 7B model text generation falling into the bottom 10 percent of benchmarks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose server configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instructions like AVX-512 and AMX. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data places the server in the average tier for general compute, cryptography, and web serving, with static web throughput reaching 12.95 GB per second. However, it exhibits weaker performance in memory-intensive tasks, with PassMark memory scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25 percent. This server is best suited for balanced workloads such as database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving, while being less optimal for memory-heavy applications or large language model text generation.
